title: Choose the Right Control
prompt: Classify each control into its functional category: Network prevention, Detection/monitoring, Endpoint and data, Deception, or Messaging and application.

items.label: NIDS: traffic copy analyzed without blocking
HIDS: agent that alerts on file changes
WAF: filtering of application-layer HTTP requests
NIPS: inline blocking of malicious traffic
Rate limiting: restricting the number of requests
EDR: behavioral detection and host isolation
DLP: blocking exfiltration of sensitive data
MDM: enforcing policy on mobile devices
XDR: correlation across endpoint, network, cloud, and identity
Honeypot: decoy system that attracts the attacker
Honeytoken: fake credential whose use is an alert signal
DMARC: SPF/DKIM alignment policy and reporting
Secrets scanning: searching for hardcoded keys in code
SELinux: mandatory access control on a Linux host

explain: Reason by layer and effect: block (prevention), alert (detection), protect the host or data (endpoint/DLP), deceive (deception), or secure messaging and code. IDS = detection, IPS = prevention: this is the most frequently tested distinction.
